title_he: הַכָּבוֹד לָאָב אֲשֶׁר הוּא אֲבִי הָאוֹרוֹת
review: 1:2 אֲבִי כָּל־הָאוֹרוֹת — 'Father of lights', the exact phrase of James 1:17 (אֲבִי הָאוֹרוֹת); the Arabic أَبُو الْأَنْوَار has the same image.

3:2–3:3 אָז יְעָדָנוּ / לִהְיוֹת דּוֹמִים לִבְנוֹ — 'He appointed us to be like His Son', for فَقَدْ عَيَّنَنَا لِنُشْبِهَ ابْنَهُ; the infinitive is post-biblical but the only way to keep the purpose clause short.
4:3–4:4 וְהִצְדִּיקָנוּ ... וְגַם כִּבְּדָנוּ — the Arabic chains 'called, justified, glorified' in one sentence (Rom 8:30); Hebrew keeps the same order and the same waw-consecutive rhythm.

5:2 אֲשֶׁר קִבַּלְנוּ בּוֹ — 'which we received in Him'; the Arabic نِلْنَاهُ فِي الْمَسِيح is a relative clause, and Hebrew keeps it relative. 'in Christ' was shortened to 'in Him' because בַּמָּשִׁיחַ overshot the line by three syllables.
